approachQuestion.prompt:
Keep the first cable record

Input: an ordered list cables of endpoint pairs (a,b). A cable is undirected: (a,b) and (b,a) describe the same cable. Self-loops (a,a) are valid. Return the original index of the first record for each distinct cable, in increasing index order.

Example 1: cables = [(3,8),(8,3),(3,3),(3,8),(8,9)]. Output: [0,2,4]. Example 2: cables = [(2,2),(2,2)]. Output: [0]. Example 3: cables = []. Output: []. 0 ≤ n ≤ 200,000.

Constraints: input is immutable; all identifiers and numeric entries are signed 32-bit integers unless specified. Arithmetic uses signed 64-bit integers. Prefer the least expected running-time growth, then avoid unnecessary asymptotic auxiliary storage. Non-adversarial hashing of fixed-size integer keys/tuples has expected amortized constant cost.

options.text: Scan records in order, using (min(a,b),max(a,b)) as a set key. Append the index only when that key has not been seen, then insert it.
options.feedback: Ordering the two endpoints creates the same key for both orientations while keeping every distinct undirected cable separate, including self-loops.

options.text: Scan with the same normalized pair keys, mapping each key to its first index and appending that index only at first insertion.
options.feedback: A map is equivalent here: it retains the same distinct keys and preserves first appearance with the same resource growth.

options.text: Use a+b as the deduplication key.
options.feedback: Cables (1,4) and (2,3) have the same sum but are different cables.

options.text: Use the original ordered pair as the set key.
options.feedback: [(3,8),(8,3)] should return [0], but ordered keys would keep both records.

feedback.reason: Canonicalize symmetric keys without collapsing distinct endpoint pairs or losing provenance.
details: Scan in input order. Normalize endpoints to an ordered min/max pair, check a set, and emit the current original index only for a previously absent key. Insert that key immediately.
Endpoints (u,v) and (v,u) describe the same cable, so normalize their order before lookup. Retain the first original record index; a sum of endpoints is not a complete pair signature.

“Scan records in order, using (min(a,b),max(a,b)) as a set key. Append the index only when that key has not been seen, then insert it.”: Ordering the two endpoints creates the same key for both orientations while keeping every distinct undirected cable separate, including self-loops.

“Use a+b as the deduplication key.”: Cables (1,4) and (2,3) have the same sum but are different cables.
“Use the original ordered pair as the set key.”: [(3,8),(8,3)] should return [0], but ordered keys would keep both records.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Keep the first cable record — analyzed method”, n is the number of cable records and u the number of distinct undirected cables. Output appends have amortized constant cost. Choose its time and auxiliary-space pair. Use the tightest standard bound for the worst legal input of size n, with expected time over non-adversarial hashing. Fixed-width integer and fixed-size tuple hash operations take expected amortized O(1); arithmetic, comparison and copying one integer take O(1). Auxiliary space excludes the supplied input and returned result, includes all maps, sets, temporary copies and call stacks. The method is iterative, with constant call-stack space.

options.text: Expected O(n + 1) time; O(u + 1) auxiliary space.
Expected O(n log n + 1) time; O(u + 1) space.

feedback.reason: Normalize one fixed-size pair and perform expected set work per record.
details: Canonicalize symmetric keys without collapsing distinct endpoint pairs or losing provenance.
Constant-size normalization and expected amortized set operations per record, plus at most n output appends, give expected O(n+1).
O(u+1) for u distinct normalized pairs and scalars. The output index array is excluded.
“Expected O(n + 1) time; O(u + 1) auxiliary space.”: Correct under the stated expected/amortized hashing model.
“Expected O(n + 1) time; O(1) space.”: The set retains u distinct normalized cable keys.
“Expected O(n log n + 1) time; O(u + 1) space.”: Normalizing two endpoints takes constant time; it does not sort the complete input.
“Expected O(n² + 1) time; O(u + 1) space.”: Each normalized pair is checked directly rather than scanned against all earlier cables.
